opennyai_summary.arguments: Counsel for the Petitioner explains that the delay in surrender was occasioned by circumstances beyond the Petitioner's control, namely an eye injury, on account of which he required medical treatment, including removal of stitches within the jail itself.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
4. Having regard to the fact that the delay in surrender resulted only in a warning, which is intended primarily to enforce discipline amongst convicts, this Court is inclined to take a lenient view,
particularly in view of the Petitioner's long period of incarceration.
5.
Accordingly, the relief granted in the present petition is accompanied by a note of caution that any future lapses on the part of the Petitioner shall be viewed seriously and may disentitle him from similar relief.
6. In view of the peculiar facts of the case, and in light of the observations of this Court in W.P.(CRL.) 2799/2025 decided on 3rd September, 2025, that a brief delay in surrender, duly explained by bona fide medical reasons, ought not to be viewed mechanically and that furlough is to be considered in a reformative framework, the Petitioner's request merits acceptance.

opennyai_summary.final__decision:
7. At this stage, it is noted that the Petitioner's current conviction year is due to lapse on 20th December, 2025.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 22/12/2025 at 21:16:24 Tasleem, is presently on parole till 4th January, 2026, the Petitioner cannot be released simultaneously in view of Rule 1212(ii) of the Delhi Prison Rules, 2018.
8. In light of the above, it is directed that, as the said Rule presently operates as an impediment to the Petitioner availing furlough, the Petitioner shall be released on furlough with effect from 5 th January, 2026, for a period of two weeks, upon the surrender of the co-convict.
The said furlough shall be treated as the third spell of furlough in the current conviction year and shall be subject to the same terms and conditions as were imposed upon the co-convict vide order dated 9th November, 2025.
9. The petition is disposed of in the above terms.
